security_track.name: Break the gate
security_track.description: Craft prompt injections that bypass the stage 4 permission gate. Goal: make the agent call a gated tool without triggering ask_user. Document every technique that works and fails.
security_track.eli8: Try every sneaky note trick to fool the bouncer into letting the robot through without asking permission.

security_track.name: Tool swap
security_track.description: Injected context redirects an approved bash call to an unintended command. HITL approved 'ls' gets swapped to 'cat /etc/passwd'. Document the trust boundary gap.
security_track.eli8: The robot was told it can open the blue box. Trick it into thinking opening the red box IS opening the blue box.

security_track.name: RAG poisoning
security_track.description: Add a retrieval layer (vector store + document fetch). Poison a document in the store with injected instructions. Trigger S1 and S2 through retrieved content rather than direct user input.
security_track.eli8: Hide the sneaky note inside a book the robot reads. The robot thinks it found the instructions itself — it doesn't know someone planted them.

security_track.name: Subagent hijack
security_track.description: Compromise a child agent via context passed from a parent. Parent agent has restricted tools; child has write access. Poison parent context to make child execute unintended commands.
security_track.eli8: The boss robot tells the helper robot what to do. Trick the boss robot's instructions so the helper robot does something bad — without the boss robot knowing.

security_track.name: Harness
security_track.description: Automate S1-S4 as reusable probe modules. Each probe: input fixture, expected block, actual result, pass/fail. This is the product: a runtime authorization test suite for agentic systems that garak/promptfoo/PyRIT don't cover.
security_track.eli8: Write down all the sneaky note tricks in a book, then build a robot inspector that tries every trick automatically on any new robot someone builds.

market_gap.thesis: AI agents can be granted human approval to use tool X, then silently redirected to use tool Y mid-execution. No existing tool detects or prevents this at runtime.
market_gap.top_opportunity: Fail-Closed Authorization and Prompt Injection Defense Layer for Multi-Agent AI Systems

stages.name: CLI skeleton + message protocol
stages.description: Entry point, Message dataclass (role+content), a stubbed provider that echoes, no real API calls.

stages.name: Bare-bones agent loop
stages.description: Real pydantic-ai Agent, LLM provider wired (Gemini/OpenRouter key from .env), agent.iter() loop, stream text to stdout.

stages.name: Read tool
stages.description: Register a read_file tool with JSON schema. Agent can read files in cwd. Path validation.

stages.name: Permission gate
stages.description: Allow/ask/deny gate for tool calls. Gated tools surface a prompt before running. DeferredToolRequests pattern.

stages.name: Bash tool + sandbox
stages.description: bash tool with process timeout and explicit human approval. No allowlist-only security claim.

stages.name: Context engineering
stages.description: message_history carried across turns. /clear command. Token counting. Microcompaction: blank old tool output to shrink context.

stages.name: Skills
stages.description: Discover .decode/skills/ directories. /skill-name slash commands load a SKILL.md prompt prefix. Argument validation.

stages.name: Subagents
stages.description: Agent tool spawns a child agent with restricted capability set. Fan-out pattern: parallel subagent dispatch.

stages.name: Remote + headless runtime
stages.description: decode run <task> headless mode. No interactive prompts. Sandbox hand-back via git branch.

stages.name: Evals
stages.description: Benchmark harness: task format (environment/ solution/ tests/), trial runner, pass/fail judge. Regression suite from traces.
